Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the draft exhibit you sent over. We did a first pass with procurement and legal and have two areas we need clarified before we can move to final sign-off: 

1) Surge cap equalization across tiers
- The current language has a per-tier surge cap that scales by slab. Our finance team is asking if we can equalize the surge cap formula so burst exposure is consistent across commitments (i.e., avoid a situation where the small tier ends up carrying disproportionate surge risk).

2) Packaging parity & smoothing
- We have a packaging question: if we migrate some SKUs between packages mid-term, how does that affect bundling/discount thresholds and the "true-up" calculation? We need an explicit tie-back so our billing system can map migrations to the correct band.

Can Redwood propose precise wording for both items or confirm that your redline will address them? Also please attach any updated exhibit + matrix you propose.

Target: we'd like to get this resolved within the week if possible.

Thanks,

Jared Silver

On Tue, Jul 22, 2025 at 11:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Jared — thanks for the clear note. Looping Karthik (legal) and Laura (RevOps) so we can propose an actionable redline and the specific billing mapping.

Team (and Jared) — I reviewed the attached exhibit and matrix. Below are proposed contract-level redlines and a short rationale. I am including two alternatives so Acme can pick the economic model they prefer.

1) Preferred approach (Option A — normalized cap by % of commitment)
- Draft language: "For purposes of surge cap equalization, per-tier surge allowance will be expressed as a percentage of the Customer's committed monthly usage for the corresponding tier. For any billing period, Redwood's per-tier surge cap shall equal 'CommittedUsageForTier * SurgePercentage', where 'SurgePercentage' is set forth in the Pricing Exhibit. This approach yields consistent relative exposure across tiers and avoids disproportionate absolute surge charges for smaller tiers."
- Rationale: clear calculation, audit-friendly, minimal bespoke exceptions.

2) Alternate approach (Option B — common band floor/ceiling)
- Draft language: "Notwithstanding tiered commitments, per-tier surge caps shall be constrained within a band defined by a floor and ceiling (e.g., 5% — 25% of monthly committed volume). Any surge above the ceiling will follow the overage rate specified in Exhibit A and be subject to quarterly true-up."
- Rationale: simpler to explain and easier for non-technical stakeholders, but may be less precise for large volume tiers.

3) Packaging parity / SKU migrations
- Add explicit mapping table (see packaging-matrix.xlsx) and a clause: "SKU migrations during a billing period will be pro-rated to the effective migration date and mapped to the target band per the Packaging Matrix. Any resulting delta will be reconciled in the next quarterly true-up."
- Also recommend an exception for rapid SKU reclassification (greater than 30% of committed volume in a quarter) to enable a commercial review, rather than automatic rebanding.

4) Operational notes for billing team (non-contractual)
- We will provide a CSV export of the mapping and a short spec for how to implement pro-rata calculations. Laura can coordinate.

If Acme prefers Option A, I will insert the Option A language into the redline and generate a track-changes PDF. If Option B is preferred, I'll draft that version instead.

Karthik Iyer
